sentences.text: Scientists estimated this creature measured roughly 1.5 meters in length.
It holds the title of the smallest known noasaurid dinosaur, surpassed only by Berthasaura.
Its anatomy included a long, slender tibia with a large flat end and very thin, rod-like second and fourth metatarsals.
A distinctive feature was that the third metatarsal served as the main bone supporting its weight.
Remains were unearthed in 1985 at Boca del Sapo in Neuquén province, Argentina.
José Bonaparte formally named and described the species Velocisaurus unicus in 1991.
Bonaparte suggested this unique foot structure evolved to help the animal run quickly.
He also proposed it was an omnivore because the claw on its fourth toe was straight instead of sharp.
A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild examined twelve foot bones and found no signs of stress fractures.
Initially, Bonaparte placed Velocisaurus in its own family called Velocisauridae.
However, in 2004, researchers reclassified it into the subfamily Noasauridae within the superfamily Abelisauroidea.
This dinosaur lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
